text:
pagerduty: Paging oncall: High 5xx/error rate detected for eu-central-2 (v6) - automatic alert triggered (network->edge). Possible MTU/PMTUD failures.

maria: saw the page, I'm on it. Initial graphs show v6 spike at 12:03UTC, ipv4 steady.

sre-bot: Alert details: service=ingress, region=eu-central-2, error_rate_v6=38%, error_rate_v4=3%, sample=12:03-12:08UTC.

maria: quick replica check -> only eu-central-2b nodes showing packet retransmit patterns on tcp flows. Uploads >8KB fail intermittently.

asha: re-routing/infra note: we recently rolled jumbo MTU to 9000 on the eu-central-2b border for an internal storage migration yesterday. Could be related.

sam: does the HTTP path prefer AAAA for these clients? We have dualstack-enabled LB edge in that AZ.

maria: yes, LB is AAAA-first for that AZ. That matches why v6 is impacted and v4 is fine.

lia: customer-suc: getting messages from 3 customers in EU about failed uploads and websocket flaps. Increasing severity.

maria: running quick tcpdump on an edge box -> seeing lots of ICMPv6 "Packet too big"? Nope, not seeing ICMP replies, just retransmits and long tails. That suggests PMTUD ICMP6 might be blocked/filtered or being lost.

asha: running `ip -6 route` and `tc qdisc` checks on border routers now. Also checking config for MTU on transit link to peer.

maria: dumping MTU on instance: `ip link show` -> eth0 mtu 9000 on affected hosts.

sam: if PMTUD ICMP6 is suppressed anywhere (middleboxes or peering) then large frames will be dropped silently. Two mitigation paths: clamp MSS on egress to 1200 on the hosts/LB, or revert MTU to 1500 on the border. Which is faster?

asha: I can push an MSS clamp on top-of-rack BGP edge quickly. Command (Juniper-style):
```
set firewall family inet6 filter CLAMP term 1 then tcp-mss 1200
commit
```
I can also apply on the Linux TCs: `tc filter add ... action pedit` but that's slower.

maria: we should do a safer mitigation first: force LB to prefer ipv4 for new connections in that AZ while we investigate. That will reduce customer impact quickly without router changes.

sam: agree. How to toggle? LB config has `prefer_ipv4` flag per-region, can flip via console API.

maria: doing it now: `curl -XPOST https://internal-api.lb/config -d '{"region":"eu-central-2","prefer_ipv4":true}'` -> response 200.

sre-bot: Automation note: preference change propagated to 32 edge nodes in ~18s.

lia: customer-suc: started emailing the 3 affected customers that we routed them to IPv4 and are investigating underlying v6 path. Included expected ETA 30m.

maria: after flip, error rate dropped from 38%->6% in the next 2 minutes. Good stopgap.

asha: trying MSS clamp on border now as follow-up to make v6 path tolerant while we find root cause. Applying clamp to egress toward peer ASN.

asha: applied tcp-mss clamp=1200 on eu-central-2b border. Monitoring.

maria: can you share BGP and interface counters?

asha: `show interfaces ge-0/0/0` -> high drops on ge-0/0/0. `show bgp summary` -> normal, no flaps. Peer MTU advertised 1500, we were sending 9000 on host side -> mismatch. Seems the transit link re-fragments/drops but not sending back ICMPv6 PTB. Peer maybe blackholing jumbos.

sam: that explains the lack of ICMPv6 PTB. If a middlebox silently drops large IPv6 fragments, clients won't get PTB and PMTUD stalls.

maria: mitigation checklist: (1) prefer ipv4 at LB (done), (2) MSS clamp applied (done), (3) revert jumbo MTU on host/border -> schedule after impact analysis, (4) open ticket with transit provider to confirm handling of IPv6 jumbo frames.

asha: kicked transit provider support and included pcap + if counters. Ticket #TP-12458. They responded that interface doesn't support jumbo egress to our peer and will drop.

maria: temporary plan: keep prefer_ipv4 while we slowly revert MTU on hosts to 1500 over the maintenance window for eu-central-2b. We'll coordinate hosts in small batches to avoid throughput regressions.

lia: customers updated, one asked for SLA credit guidance. I'm collecting affected request IDs; lia->maria can you attach logs?

maria: attaching sample request-ids: r-11a2, r-11a3, r-11b8. Logs show TCP retransmits and zero ICMPv6 PTB.

sre-bot: Incident severity escalated to SEV2 based on customer impact.

sam: preparing postmortem items: evaluate why we enabled jumbo for that cluster without verifying transit, add monitoring for ICMPv6 PTB rate, and add runbook step to auto-MSS-clamp when v6 large-packet failures are detected.

asha: rolling MTU revert plan: reduce host MTU to 1500 on a small subset (5 nodes) now to confirm no regressions. Command: `sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500`. Doing it via orchestration job.

maria: handoff to night oncall (asha) at 12:30UTC. I'll remain reachable for coordination.

asha: acknowledged handoff. Will keep prefer_ipv4 in place until MTU revert completes and transit confirms. Will follow up with transit and update this thread.

maria: tl;dr customer impact on eu-central-2b v6 path due to mismatch/jumbo frames + dropped ICMPv6 PTB. Rapid mitigations: LB prefer_ipv4 -> immediate drop in errors; MSS clamp on border; MTU revert in progress; transit vendor engaged.

lia: closing loop with customers now that traffic stabilized; sending follow-up note with interim mitigation and ETA for root cause fix.

sre-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. SEV2 -> postmortem pending.

asha: will post final notes and RCA in #postmortems when complete.

maria: thanks all. I'll add action items to the postmortem: verify jumbo rollout process, add PMTUD/alive checks, and make prefer_ipv4 toggle part of the oncall runbook for v6 outages.

asha: update 12:48UTC: MTU revert completed on first batch (5 nodes) no regression, continuing.

maria: last check 12:52UTC: overall error rate back to baseline on both stacks, switching incident to status: resolved->monitoring.

sre-bot: Incident resolved at 12:52UTC. Postmortem: assign to asha and sam.

(incident-thread ends)
